6.0.0.en: The Lamb opened: that is, Christ alone has the right to declare what He wants to declare to His creation, and the phrase opened a seal also indicates that He discloses to us a trick or a problem that may hinder a person from reaching God.

6.0.1.en: I heard one: the first of the angelic creatures (of the four beasts) called to John with a loud voice, as it were the noise of thunder, a voice that accords with his form (like a lion), and this strong voice was a warning of the importance of what John was about to see.

6.1.0.en: A white horse: the white horse points to victory, since the Roman commanders were accustomed to ride decorated white horses when they returned triumphant, and here the horse represents the Church with her pure apostles and her saints, for since she carries her Christ (the one sitting on it), victory has become assured to her in Him and by Him.

6.1.1.en: He that sat on him: He is Christ Himself, the secret of the Church's strength and victory; "a bow was given unto him," that is, He fights her wars and gains the victory for her (Ex 14:14), and "a crown was given unto him" because He is her only King and the Controller of all her affairs. Conquering, and to conquer: that is, victory is an essential attribute in Him and not something added to Him, and it also means that He is not like anyone else who may conquer at one time and be conquered at another.

6.1.2.en: Since the seals following this seal carried kinds of suffering and striving against evil, and woes about to come, God wanted to reassure His loving children who hold fast to their faith, so the opening of the first seal came encouraging, speaking of the victory and its completion and the assured triumph of the Church by her Christ, her leader... and these words are for all of us.

6.1.3.en: If the wars or the sufferings of the Church grow severe, we must not faint or be shaken or let our confidence in Christ weaken; we only need to remember these words "conquering, and to conquer," and hope returns and confidence returns to us. Note: some may ask how the Lamb who opened the book can be Christ and also the One who sits on the throne be Christ... and here we return to the saying that all these scenes are spiritual, heavenly and symbolic, and the proof of that is that the Lord Christ declares Himself in the Book of Revelation in more than one form and with more than one attribute and appearance.

6.2.0.en: The second angel (like a calf, ch. 4:7) called out like what the first called out, summoning St. John to look and contemplate.

6.3.0.en: After the scene of the first horse came reassuring.. the scene of the second horse came disturbing, for its color is red, that is, bloody, and the one sitting on it is the authority of evil and he has great power (a great sword). He will stir up persecutions against the Church, and also many wars in all generations until people long for peace and no one finds it except the one who has put his hope and confidence in Christ.. and this horse and its rider agree with all that the Lord Christ said and foretold in His discourse recorded in (Mt 24); it represents the different ages of persecution in which a great number of Christians are martyred.

6.3.1.en: "Was given": it indicates that although wars are the doing of men and the thought of Satan, they are by God's permission, and perhaps He intended by them discipline, repentance and return.

6.3.2.en: The martyrs have a great standing in the Church because they offered their whole lives for the sake of Christ. So try to bear the tribulations you pass through and give up some of your desires for the sake of love and peace, and so win souls for Christ.

6.4.0.en: The scene of calling to St. John is repeated, and the one who calls here is the third being, whose face was as a man (ch. 4:7). A black horse: it points to death because of the famines coming upon the world.

6.4.1.en: A pair of balances in his hand: the balance signifies hunger.., for instead of using the measure, which signifies abundance of grain, he uses the balance, which signifies scarcity and the dividing of food by weight, and this accords with what Ezekiel also prophesied, "Behold, I will break the staff of bread in Jerusalem: and they shall eat bread by weight" (Ezek 4:16).

6.5.0.en: A further clarification and description of the picture of the hunger and famines to come.

6.5.1.en: "A measure of wheat": that is, the price of a quantity of wheat (a Greek unit), which is the least possible amount on which a person can live on bread in one day, and the penny is the wage of a whole day (Mt 20:9), and the meaning is that a person's wage for a day will not be enough for him for one day's bread.

6.5.2.en: "Three measures of barley": barley is the food of the poor and a bread worse than wheat bread is made from it.. and the meaning is that even barley bread will not be available but a person will get it with difficulty. And see thou hurt not the oil and the wine: despite the famine and hunger about to come upon the world and the authority of this horseman, he will not be able to take away from the Church her joy (her wine) or the work of the Holy Spirit (her oil). The spiritual meaning in all this is that besides the real famines that come upon the world from time to time, there is also death and perdition (a black horse) as a result of man's hunger for the word of God and his poverty of it, but God always keeps His mercies for the one who takes refuge in Him by the work of His Holy Spirit within him and his constant satisfaction with His most holy Blood, which is symbolized (by the wine).

6.5.3.en: Before difficult times come in which the word of God is scarce, such as your being busy with many things, or your being struck with illnesses, or persecutions arising, seize the opportunity now and care about reading the Holy Bible and attending the spiritual meetings, and enjoy partaking of the Holy Mysteries.

6.6.0.en: At the opening of the fourth seal the fourth beast (like an eagle) (ch. 4:7) called out like those before him, "Come and see," and what St. John saw was:

6.6.1.en: A pale horse: in the English translation and others it is called the Pale-hourse, and it is a reference to a heresy and a heterodoxy brought forth by the person of an impostor, and because of his seriousness he is called "Death," and Death is not only a name for him but also the end of whoever follows him and follows his faith.

6.6.2.en: Hell followed with him: hell (Hades) means the abode of the dead, and it also signifies the place of the forces of evil; and the meaning is that the destiny of whoever accepts this teaching, strange to the faith, is death and perdition; and the author of this heresy (the strange faith) will use all available means to fight the faith of the children of God, such as killing by the sword to spread his claim, or starvation and persecution.

6.6.3.en: With the beasts of the earth: that is, his followers, and the word beasts was used to indicate the harshness of their natures and the severity of their ravaging of the peoples they enter and whose goods they drain.

6.6.4.en: Power over the fourth part of the earth: that is, God's mercies did not allow the heresy of this deceiver to spread over more than a quarter of the earth, for God is the keeper of the faith of His children, and however fierce and destructive the danger, it is limited before His power.

6.6.5.en: My beloved brother... this pale horse is frightening... do you not see with me that it has swallowed many (a quarter of the earth), so be on guard and guard your house and your children against any strange faith that the Church of Christ does not teach in her sound faith, and do not forget that its name is Death and Hell follows with it.

6.7.s.en: (5) The fifth seal and the new vision

6.7.0.en: The souls of them that were slain: everyone who accepted suffering and martyrdom for the sake of the faith and the word of truth. Under the altar: since the altar is the holiest place in the life of the Church, where the believer meets Christ the Sacrifice, the Redeemer and the Savior, so God assigned the martyrs the holiest similar place in heaven, where Christ's constant and continual presence is, that is, they are the nearest of people in standing to Him, as compensation for their sufferings, for everyone who lays down his life for God becomes the nearest of people to Him and the most enjoying of Him.

6.8.0.en: They cried with a loud voice: we understand from these words the following...

6.8.1.en: 1- That the saints who are in heaven have feelings, for the crying comes as an expression of feeling.

6.8.2.en: 2- That they know what happens on earth and that heaven is an extension of their life, for they have not forgotten what happened to them.

6.8.3.en: 3- God permits the saints in heaven to speak with Him, and He answers them also (v. 11). For this reason our doctrine of the intercession of the saints is an expression of a scriptural faith, since they have not been separated from us but the form of their life has changed, so that they are occupied with nothing but God, speaking with Him and remembering us before Him. How long, O Lord... dost thou not judge and avenge our blood: it is not fitting to say that the souls of the saints carry with them in heaven the desire for revenge.. rather it is a communion with the divine justice that comes near to prayer... as the prophet David said, "How long wilt thou forget me, O LORD?" (Ps 13), and this communion and prayer in its meaning is a declaration from God to us that He does not forget the blood of His children, as He said to Cain, "the voice of thy brother's blood crieth unto me" (Gen 4:10). We can also say that these holy martyrs do not ask vengeance on particular people but vengeance on the whole kingdom of evil, and this is of course permissible spiritually.

6.9.0.en: God did not answer their request at the beginning, but rewarded them with a great heavenly reward: He first clothed them with white robes as a symbol of joy, purity and holiness, then gave them rest out of the overflow of His love.

6.9.1.en: A little season: that is, they will wait in this state of glory and rest for a little time compared with the glories of eternity.

6.9.2.en: Until their fellowservants should be fulfilled: here God's answer to their question "How long?..." came, for God teaches them that the time of the striving Church is not yet complete.. and there are still some persecutions that reach the point of martyrdom.. but when the appointed time comes and the Church completes her witness, the general resurrection comes and the judgment of the wicked and the reward of the righteous are revealed.

6.9.3.en: May we not be shaken by what the Church passes through of suffering... for this is her portion as long as she remains a witness for Christ against the world, but let us put all our confidence and hope in Christ and His promises, and know that in the plan of His wisdom there is a time to every purpose under the heaven... so let us be strengthened by patience and confidence in God's just recompense, and may God give us grace to complete the days of our sojourn in peace.

6.10.s.en: (6) The sixth seal and the end of time

6.10.0.en: This scene carries a vision joined to the conditions of the end of the world before the second coming of the Lord, and it completes what Christ foretold in (Mt 24). A great earthquake: that is, a great, frightening shaking that suits and corresponds to the event about to take place, and it signifies the shaking of the faith of many.

6.10.1.en: The sun became black: that is, the disappearance of the sky and of all light, and thick darkness became the prevailing thing, and this increases the sadness and terror of the scene. The sun signifies Christ, that is, Christ hid His knowledge from many because of their persistence in sin.

6.10.2.en: The moon became as blood: that is, whoever seeks a little light after the disappearance of the sun will not find it. The moon also signifies the Church, as the Song of Songs describes her, "fair as the moon" (Song 6:10), and so its turning into blood means that the Church is filled with martyrs.

6.11.0.en: As figs or any other fruit fall before the violent winds, so the stars of heaven fall and all nature dissolves) ... see what the Lord said in Mt 24:29) and the stars signify leaders in the Church who fall and depart from the faith, like the heretics.

6.12.0.en: St. John continues describing the scene that is to happen; after the elements of material life and the nature we are familiar with have passed away, heaven opens like a book that was closed and rolled up, and this comparison means that what was hidden, like the writing inside the roll of the scroll, God will declare to all. Every mountain and island were moved out of their places: the direct meaning can be joined to the signs of the end of the world, for after the passing of the sun, the moon and the stars, so the mountains pass away and the islands are moved as a result of the end of gravity with the passing of the sun. But the spiritual meaning is closer here, for the mountains and islands point to the kingdoms of the world, whether lofty like mountains or many and scattered like islands, which have no stability or value before the coming of the fearful Lord, and this meaning accords more with the spiritual description in the next verse.

6.13.0.en: The kings of the earth, and the great men, and the rich men, and the chief captains, and the mighty men: they are everyone from whom people expected steadfastness before hardships and escape from them because of their strength, their abundant money and their earthly authority.

6.13.1.en: Every bondman, and every free man: that is, all the remaining classes in society, what applied to the former will apply to them.

6.13.2.en: Hid themselves in the dens: a figurative expression whose purpose is to show the intensity of fear and terror and the desire to flee and hide while this is not available; for how can a person hide or find a way after the falling of the stars and the disappearance of the sun and the moon... or how can a person hide from the face of God?!

6.13.3.en: And the meaning is that everything a person boasts of, whether leadership or rank or abundant money or mental ability, will not profit a person at all.

6.13.4.en: Remember with me, beloved, that only the humble find favour with God (Lk 1:30), so may we learn to glory in nothing but God Himself and our relation to Him (2 Cor 10:17).

6.14.0.en: From the terror of the scene and its intensity for those not prepared to meet the heavenly Bridegroom, they wish for death or final disappearance and find nothing of this, so they cry out, addressing the mountains and rocks to fall on them so that they may not face God the Father (who sits on the throne) or God the Son (the Lamb), for they have known by the Spirit that this is the day of His wrath, that is, the day of His second coming and the revealing of His just judgment upon them, and who is able to stand or defend himself on this day, He before whom "every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty" (Rom 3:19).

6.14.1.en: The rite of the Church carries many spiritual meanings in its movements.. for at the end of the Liturgy the priest carries the Body of Christ in the paten, placing it twice in two circuits that represent two comings of the Lord Christ, the first for redemption and mercy.. and the second for the just judgment, and the people cry out in both circuits "Blessed is He that cometh in the name of the Lord," reverently and prostrating, expressing the fear of this wonderful day, the day of the second coming of Christ... Have mercy on us, Lord... and have mercy again.

6.14.2.en: The sealing of the believers, an introduction to the seventh chapter: this chapter came as an interlude between the sixth chapter, in which the six seals were opened, and the eighth chapter, which speaks of the opening of the seventh and last seal, and since the last thing that came in the sixth seal was frightening and what will also be declared in the eighth chapter is awesome, the seventh chapter came between them to reassure the children of God and to tell them of a mark that is specially theirs, and also a picture of their heavenly inheritance.
